statement: The interior angles of a convex polygon add up to $2340^\circ$. How many diagonals does the polygon have?

choices.misconception: I found that the polygon has 15 sides and then counted only the 12 diagonals that start at one vertex.
I divided 2340 by 180 to get 13 sides and forgot that the angle sum is (n - 2) times 180, then used 13 times 10 over 2.
I counted every pair of vertices, 15 choose 2, which also counts the 15 sides as if they were diagonals.
I used n(n - 3) = 15 times 12 and forgot to divide by 2, so every diagonal was counted from both of its ends.

hints: Start by finding the number of sides.
The interior angles of an $n$-gon sum to $(n-2)\cdot 180^\circ$. Each vertex sends a diagonal to every vertex except itself and its two neighbours.
$(n-2)\cdot 180 = 2340$ gives $n - 2 = 13$, so $n = 15$. Each vertex starts $15 - 3 = 12$ diagonals, and each diagonal has two ends, so there are $\frac{15 \cdot 12}{2}$ of them.

solutions.reliable: Solve $(n-2)\cdot 180 = 2340$: $n - 2 = 13$, so $n = 15$. From each of the 15 vertices there are $15 - 3 = 12$ diagonals (every other vertex except the two neighbours). Counting this way reaches each diagonal twice, once from each end, so the total is $\frac{15 \cdot 12}{2} = 90$. Transferable idea: count from one point, then divide by how many times each object was counted.
solutions.elegant: Diagonals are the pairs of vertices that are not sides: $\binom{15}{2} - 15 = 105 - 15 = 90$. Transferable idea: count everything, then subtract what is not wanted.
